title: Uncaught AddrInUse when restarting server in watch mode after saving file

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Having this issue too. I can't use --watch with an express server because it says the port is in use after the first restart.

I think deno is _too fast_ and it restarts the app before the express server can release the port.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: I don't think it's time bound after doing some tests. I think maybe an issue with the `beforeExit` event not firing?

comments.body: The fix is in https://github.com/denoland/deno/pull/16616. I'll try to land that PR tonight.

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
I ran into the same problem on 1.31.1, upgraded to 1.31.2 with fingers crossed, but same thing.

As a workaround to the problem, this seems to work for me.

```ts
import { Server } from 'https://deno.land/std@0.179.0/http/server.ts'

const handler = () => new Response('Hello World!')
const hostname = 'localhost'
const port = 8080

const server = new Server({ hostname, port, handler })
console.log(`Starting to listen on port ${port}`)
server.listenAndServe()

globalThis.addEventListener('unload', () => {
  server.close()
})
```

comments.author: reporter
participant14
comments.body:
For brew users, the workaround is:

```bash
# the cask version that pointed to deno@1.30.0
FORMULA_URL='https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/2b3035ebfc70660dc8753678b43404d5d8016f99/Formula/deno.rb'
# get the .rb file locally
curl -O $FORMULA_URL
# replace the installed deno with the v1.30.0 version
brew uninstall deno
brew install ./deno.rb
```

Chiming in that this is reproducable in Deno 2.0.0, I'm also using Signal Listeners for `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM` to gracefully shut down the server and remove the UNIX domain socket file that `.serve()` is running on, but when running with `--watch` the server exits immidiately without letting my handlers clean up. 

If this is intentional behavior then there should be documentation on the proper way to clean up `.sock` files when exiting and using `--watch` in development.
